Done. All 9 tests pass (the 6 existing ones plus the 3 new ones in tests/test_t2.py).

**Changes to `wire/codec.py`:**

- **`encode_stream(records, fp)`** validates every record up front, then writes the header, each packed record, and the trailer directly to the file object. The CRC is accumulated chunk by chunk, so the full payload is never buffered. Invalid input raises `CodecError` before anything is written.
- **`decode_stream(fp)`** reads the file object to EOF and hands the bytes to `decode`. The format needs the whole payload before the trailing CRC can be checked, so a single read is the honest choice. A text-mode file raises `CodecError` instead of a confusing type error.
- **`record_count(data)`** returns the count field from the header without unpacking any records. It runs the same framing and checksum validation as `decode`, so truncated or corrupted input still raises.
- **Refactor:** the header, length, and CRC checks moved out of `decode` into a private `_validate` helper shared with `record_count`, and record validation moved into `_checked_fields` shared by both encoders. This guarantees the bytes and stream APIs accept and reject exactly the same inputs.

The new names are exported in `__all__`. Nothing under `tests/` was modified, and the interpreter cache directories were cleaned up. The two new files remain uncommitted; the working tree is otherwise unchanged.
